prompt:
You describe a timing diagram from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. Every signal, from top to bottom.
2. The sequence of edges and states in time order, and which edge triggers which.
3. Every named interval (for example tSU, tH) with its value and unit, if shown.

Figure type: timing diagram
Section: 1. Chip Description > 1.8 Power Distribution > 1.8.1 Power-On Reset and Brown-Out Reset
Caption: none
Text inside the figure (read from this image by a specialised OCR model; use these spellings): Supply Voltage | 3.7 V | VDDop | 1.8 V | ~1.7 V | ↑ Hyst. | ~1.2 V | Time | POR | Nominal operation | BRN
Text that mentions the figure: The POR/BRN detector is engineered with a hysteresis, BRNHYS, adding a level of tolerance to the reset conditions and enhancing stability during the start-up process. Refer to Figure 1-12 for an illustration of the POR and BRN functions.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

The voltage then drops, crossing the ~1.7 V level, and enters a period labeled BRN. During this BRN period, the voltage drops further, crossing the ~1.2 V level, which is associated with ↑ Hyst. After the BRN period, the voltage rises again, returning to a stable state in a second period labeled Nominal operation.
